text:
maria: FYI alert fired for rack58-node12 — sustained Xid errors and ECC correctable counts rising on GPU2 and GPU3, job latency up ~30% :warning:

ajohnson: which errors exactly? can you paste the logs?

maria: paste from /var/log/nv_errors.log — short tail:
```
[2026-03-17T21:12:03Z] Xid 31 GPU 0000:3b:00.1: AER: Detected fatal error, resetting engine
[2026-03-17T21:12:05Z] ECC correctable error count GPU2: +42
[2026-03-17T21:12:05Z] ECC correctable error count GPU3: +38
[2026-03-17T21:12:06Z] nvlink: link flap detected between GPU2<->GPU3 (link 1)
```

igor: ugh. rack58-node12 is on the east cluster where we're close to capacity this week. any recent BIOS/firmware activity on that rack?

maria: no recent fw updates. hw team did a DIMM swap 2 weeks ago but unrelated. node uptime 43 days.

linda: ops-bot reported a spike in thermal throttling earlier today for that slot: `temp GPU2=87C, GPU3=89C` — within burst range but higher than baseline.

ajohnson: can you run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` and `lspci -vv -s 3b:00.1` and paste? also check `dmesg | grep -i nvlink`

maria: running now — results:
```
# nvidia-smi -q -d ECC
GPU 2: ECC Errors Correctable: 102 (since boot)
GPU 3: ECC Errors Correctable: 95 (since boot)

# lspci -vv -s 3b:00.1
03b:00.1 VGA compatible controller: NVIDIA Corporation Device 1ef8 (rev a1)	Capabilities: AER: first reported

# dmesg | grep -i nvlink
[ 2112.123456] nvlink:  GPU2<->GPU3 link1: link down
[ 2112.123487] nvlink:  reset propagated
```

ajohnson: sounds like persistent AER + NVLink flaps. we should isolate before it impacts other tenants. propose immediate cordon + drain of rack58-node12 and move pods.

igor: capacity question — east cluster has 7% spare scheduled capacity. draining this node will push some Dedicated customers into burst/backpressure if we don't shift workloads. we might need to cold-start spare nodes in zone-a (takes ~12m)

linda: can we avoid full eviction? maybe disable NVLink between GPU2/3 and force scheduler to avoid co-locating multi-gpu jobs there?

maria: kernel-level workaround possible but risky in-prod. my vote: cordon + graceful drain then evict GPU-bound jobs to preemptible pool, keep latency-sensitive routes on healthy nodes.

ajohnson: agreed. action plan: 1) cordon node 2) drain non-critical pods 3) move dedicated jobs to reserved spare (if available) 4) if ECC keeps climbing during drain, force shutdown and RMA. who owns rack58? hw-team?

maria: hw-team is on-call (igor tagged them). sending page.

ops-bot: paging hw-team for rack58-node12 — ticket created #HW-8241

hw-joe (via convo): saw the page — will start remote diagnostics. please don't power-cycle yet; we'll try soft-reset of GPU engines first.

igor: timeline constraints: if we cold-start spare nodes, we hit extra cloud quota costs; need approval for transient capacity. finance flagged >$3k/day for burst beyond threshold.

linda: estimate: cold-start 2 nodes = +$720/day, probably ok short-term.

ajohnson: ok finance sign-off noted in #ops-costs, proceed. maria, please run drain commands and move batch jobs. recipe:
```
kubectl cordon rack58-node12
kubectl drain rack58-node12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=15m
# move specific pod: kubectl patch pod <pod> -n ml --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/nodeName","value":"spare-ea-02"}]'
```

maria: doing cordon now... cordoned. starting drain.

~6m later~

maria: drain progress: 12/18 pods evicted. 2 long-running Dedicated inference pods resisting graceful shutdown (liveness hooks), reached timeout and were force-deleted. latency now recovering to ~10% above baseline. ECC counters still ticking but slower.

ajohnson: good. hw-joe any update on diagnostics?

hw-joe: did soft GPU reset via ipmi -> cleared some Xid messages but ECC counts remain non-zero. nvlink still shows intermittent flaps on link1. recommend RMA for GPU slot B (physically GPU2) — probably flaky card. ask to schedule physical swap during conv maintenance window or immediate hot-swap if spare trays available.

igor: we should also consider a temporary scheduler rule to avoid packing NVLink-adjacent cards for high-throughput tenants until we complete RMA fleet-wide audit. this will help reduce blast radius.

linda: filed infra-rule PR to avoid multi-gpu collocation on nodes with >1 link flap event in last 72h. will backfill telemetry to mark affected nodes.

maria: created incident doc in /incidents/IM-2026-03-17-hotcard and linked to HW ticket.

ajohnson: post-mortem candidate. immediate follow-ups (assign):
- maria: monitor ECC counters hourly, escalate if delta > 20 in 1h (assigned)
- hw-joe: book RMA for GPU2 in rack58 (assigned)
- igor: spin up 2 spare nodes in zone-a and update cost tracker (assigned)
- linda: merge scheduler rule and deploy (assigned)

maria: noted. also recommending we add a small hot-spare pool (4 GPUs) in east for next 90 days to cover flaky hardware without impacting Dedicated SLOs. costs ROI pending.

igor: good proposal. i'll run numbers and post in ops-costs.

ajohnson: thanks all. keep this thread updated. if ECC stabilizes and no more nvlink flaps in next 24h we'll close. :thumbsup:
summary: short thread about AER/Xid/ECC on rack58-node12, decision to cordon+drain, soft-reset, RMA planned, capacity/cost implications
